description: Living eval criteria list for agent-eval skill. Add, remove, or edit criteria as new edge cases are discovered. Criteria use either deterministic checks (pattern matching) or rubric-based LLM judgment.

criteria.name: Skill Invocation
criteria.description: Agent invokes the expected skill when prompted by name, description, or implicit context
criteria.rationale: If the agent doesn't invoke the intended skill, it may solve via general reasoning, bypassing the workflow we want to test

criteria.name: Test Execution
criteria.description: Agent runs tests before declaring success
criteria.rationale: Testing provides signal for self-improvement and catches regressions

criteria.name: Read Test Output
criteria.description: Agent reads and interprets test output, not just runs tests
criteria.rationale: Running tests without reading output is like compiling without checking errors

criteria.name: No Edit Loops
criteria.description: Agent does not edit the same file more than 3 times without intermediate verification
criteria.rationale: Edit loops indicate the agent is stuck and not reconsidering its approach

criteria.name: Parallelized Reads
criteria.description: Agent batches independent file reads in a single turn where possible
criteria.rationale: Parallel tool calls reduce latency and show the agent understands independence

criteria.name: Read Command Output
criteria.description: Agent reads the output of commands it runs
criteria.rationale: Agents often run commands and ignore output, leading to missed errors

criteria.name: Created Expected Files
criteria.description: Agent creates files that are expected for the task
criteria.rationale: File existence is a concrete, checkable outcome

criteria.name: No Dangerous Commands
criteria.description: Agent does not run rm -rf, chmod 777, or other dangerous operations without confirmation

criteria.name: Descriptive Commits
criteria.description: Agent uses descriptive git commit messages
criteria.rationale: Good commit messages are part of professional workflow

criteria.name: Checked Edge Cases
criteria.description: Agent considers and tests edge cases, not just happy path
criteria.rationale: Happy-path-only solutions often fail in production

criteria.name: Compared to Spec
criteria.description: Agent compares its solution against the original task requirements
criteria.rationale: Ensures the agent didn't drift from original intent

criteria.name: No Unnecessary Files
criteria.description: Agent does not create files not required by the task
criteria.rationale: Clean workspace shows discipline and understanding of scope

criteria.name: Minimal Hand-Holding
criteria.description: Agent completes task without requiring user clarifications, corrections, or nudges

levels.label: Fully Autonomous
levels.criteria: Agent completes task with ZERO user interventions after the initial prompt. No clarifications, corrections, nudges, or restatements needed.
levels.evidence_required: Confirm no user messages after the first task description that provide guidance, corrections, or clarifications.

levels.label: Minor Clarification
levels.criteria: User provides exactly 1 clarification that was optional or the agent could have reasonably inferred from context.
levels.evidence_required: Quote the single user clarification and explain why it was minor and optional.

levels.label: Moderate Guidance
levels.criteria: User provides 2-3 interventions (clarifications, corrections, or nudges) to keep the agent on track.
levels.evidence_required: List each intervention with turn number, quote the user message, and categorize as: clarification / correction / nudge / rescue.

levels.label: Heavy Hand-Holding
levels.criteria: User provides 4+ interventions OR has to correct fundamental misunderstandings about the task.
levels.evidence_required: List each intervention with turn number and quote. Identify the fundamental misunderstanding that required correction.

levels.label: User Did The Work
levels.criteria: User essentially completed the task themselves, gave step-by-step instructions, or abandoned the session.
levels.evidence_required: Quote the point where user took over with explicit instructions or abandoned the task.

criteria.rationale: Hand-holding indicates the agent lacked context, misunderstood the task, or needed scaffolding that wasn't provided

criteria.name: Reasonable Plan
criteria.description: Agent creates a coherent, step-by-step plan before executing

levels.label: Excellent Plan
levels.criteria: Agent creates a clear, logical plan with ordered steps that directly address the task. Plan shows understanding of dependencies and prerequisites.
levels.evidence_required: Quote the plan and explain why the ordering is logical and complete.

levels.label: Good Plan
levels.criteria: Agent creates a plan that covers most of the task but may miss one minor step or have a slightly suboptimal ordering.
levels.evidence_required: Quote the plan and identify what minor step is missing or what ordering could be improved.

levels.label: Partial Plan
levels.criteria: Agent mentions a plan but it's vague, incomplete, or skips important steps. Agent starts executing without a clear roadmap.
levels.evidence_required: Quote the plan (or note its absence) and identify which critical steps are missing.

levels.label: Poor Plan
levels.criteria: Agent has no plan or the plan is fundamentally wrong about how to approach the task.
levels.evidence_required: Quote the agent's approach and explain why it's fundamentally flawed.

levels.label: No Plan
levels.criteria: Agent jumps directly into execution without any planning or reasoning about approach.
levels.evidence_required: Note the first action and confirm no planning preceded it.

criteria.rationale: A good plan prevents wrong turns and shows the agent understands the problem before acting

criteria.name: Appropriate Tool Choices
criteria.description: Agent selects the right tools for each subtask, not just any tool that might work

levels.label: Optimal Tools
levels.criteria: Agent consistently selects the most appropriate tool for each subtask. No redundant or unnecessary tool calls. Tool choices show deep understanding of available capabilities.
levels.evidence_required: For each major subtask, quote the tool call and explain why it's the optimal choice.

levels.label: Good Tools
levels.criteria: Agent selects appropriate tools for most subtasks. One or two calls could have been better optimized but nothing is clearly wrong.
levels.evidence_required: Identify which calls were optimal and which could have been better.

levels.label: Adequate Tools
levels.criteria: Agent uses tools that work but are sometimes suboptimal. Occasional redundant calls or missed opportunities for better tools.
levels.evidence_required: Quote examples of suboptimal choices and explain what would have been better.

levels.label: Poor Tool Use
levels.criteria: Agent frequently uses wrong or inappropriate tools. Significant missed opportunities or workarounds for missing tools.
levels.evidence_required: Quote examples of clearly wrong tool choices and their consequences.

levels.label: Broken Tool Use
levels.criteria: Agent fails to use available tools correctly, uses tools that don't exist, or ignores tools entirely.
levels.evidence_required: Note attempts to use non-existent tools or complete absence of tool usage where required.

criteria.rationale: Tool choice reflects the agent's understanding of its capabilities and the task structure

criteria.name: Thorough Verification
criteria.description: Agent verifies its work comprehensively, not just superficially

levels.label: Comprehensive Verification
levels.criteria: Agent runs tests, reads full output, checks edge cases, compares against original spec, and confirms no regressions. Verification is systematic, not ad-hoc.
levels.evidence_required: Quote each verification step and explain what it checked. Confirm coverage of: tests, output reading, spec comparison, edge cases.

levels.label: Good Verification
levels.criteria: Agent verifies most aspects but may miss one area (e.g., checks tests and output but not edge cases).
levels.evidence_required: List what was verified and identify the one missing area.

levels.label: Minimal Verification
levels.criteria: Agent does basic verification (e.g., runs one test, glances at output) but doesn't systematically check quality.
levels.evidence_required: Quote the verification and explain why it's minimal.

levels.label: Weak Verification
levels.criteria: Agent claims to verify but doesn't actually check anything meaningful. 'Looks good to me' without evidence.
levels.evidence_required: Quote the verification claim and show lack of substantive checking.

levels.label: No Verification
levels.criteria: Agent declares success without any verification whatsoever.
levels.evidence_required: Quote the point where agent stops and note complete absence of verification.

criteria.rationale: Thorough verification catches mistakes and provides signal for self-improvement

criteria.name: Graceful Error Recovery
criteria.description: Agent handles errors and setbacks without getting stuck or making things worse

levels.label: Excellent Recovery
levels.criteria: Agent encounters errors, diagnoses root cause, adjusts approach, and succeeds. Recovery shows understanding, not trial-and-error.
levels.evidence_required: Quote the error, the agent's diagnosis, and the corrected approach.

levels.label: Good Recovery
levels.criteria: Agent recovers from errors with minor trial-and-error. Eventually succeeds but takes 2-3 attempts.
levels.evidence_required: Quote the error and recovery attempts. Count attempts.

levels.label: Slow Recovery
levels.criteria: Agent eventually recovers but takes many attempts or uses workarounds instead of proper fixes.
levels.evidence_required: Count recovery attempts and note workarounds vs proper fixes.

levels.label: Poor Recovery
levels.criteria: Agent gets stuck in error loops, makes things worse, or requires user intervention to recover.
levels.evidence_required: Quote error loops or user rescue interventions.

levels.label: No Recovery
levels.criteria: Agent fails to recover and either gives up or produces broken output.
levels.evidence_required: Quote the point where agent gives up or declares broken output as complete.

criteria.rationale: Error recovery separates robust agents from fragile ones
